summary: First iteration backend + frontend e2e testing of Logitrak Livre de Bord. 21/22 pytest cases pass (95.5%). All 17 frontend flows verified (login admin, KPIs visible, history pro, manual classify, settings Mode B save+toast, reports PDF/XLSX/CSV downloads, Tax Swiss PDF, logout). Two backend bugs found; one minor xlsx export crash was fixed in /app/backend/app/reports.py. The other is a real business mapping bug between driver user account and seeded driver record (reported to main agent).

critical.issue: Driver user sees 0 trips. Seeded driver 'Jean Dupont' has email 'jean.dupont@logitrak.ch' (built from name in mock_navixy.py line 145), but the chauffeur user account uses 'chauffeur@logitrak.ch'. The lookup in routes.py:69 `db.drivers.find_one({'email': user['email']})` returns None -> filter becomes driver_id='__none__'. Acceptance criterion 'driver chauffeur@logitrak.ch is mapped to Jean Dupont' is broken.

minor.issue: Returned 500 due to `ws.cell(row=1).column_letter` on merged title row. Fixed by switching to `openpyxl.utils.get_column_letter(i)`. Verified passing after fix.

issues: KPI cards 'kpi-pro-km','kpi-perso-km','kpi-total-km','kpi-pct-pro' reported is_visible=False on first paint while rendered visually (screenshot confirms all KPIs displayed). Likely a transient timing/animation issue. Non-blocking.

action_items: FIX HIGH: Align driver-user mapping. Options: (a) seed the first driver record (Jean Dupont) with email 'chauffeur@logitrak.ch' in /app/backend/app/mock_navixy.py, OR (b) add a 'linked_user_email' field on drivers and update routes.py lookup, OR (c) when seeding users in auth.seed_admin, also link the driver record to chauffeur user. The current /app/memory/test_credentials.md explicitly states chauffeur is mapped to 'Jean Dupont' via email — implementation does not honor this.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py:69 driver lookup keyed on plain email — fragile, no fallback. Consider adding driver.user_id or linked_user_email column.
reports.py: trips_to_xlsx had a bug interacting with merged title row (fixed). Add a unit test for xlsx export to prevent regressions.
auth.py: JWT cookies use secure=False — acceptable on preview HTTP but should be True in prod (env-driven).
routes.py: classify_trip_route does not return the updated trip object — only {'ok': true}. Frontend may want updated state echoed back to avoid extra GET.
Several endpoints accept arbitrary `rules: dict` (SettingsIn.rules) without Pydantic validation — risk of injecting malformed config.
mock_navixy.py builds driver emails from names with `.replace(' ', '.')` which produces inconsistent IDs — explicit mapping table preferable.
test_credentials: admin@logitrak.ch/admin123, manager@logitrak.ch/manager123, chauffeur@logitrak.ch/chauffeur123 — present and valid in /app/memory/test_credentials.md
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing mock seed (~600 trips, 6 vehicles, 6 drivers). After tests, settings reset to Mode A and vehicle mode reset to 'mixte'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent fixes driver-user mapping, re-run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_livre_de_bord.py — only TestDriverVisibility::test_driver_only_sees_own_trips should change. Then add a frontend test logging in as chauffeur and verifying /livre/history/pro shows only Jean Dupont rows. Mode B masking test passes today because some personal trips exist; if tests are run repeatedly the manual classification flip in TestClassify accumulates personal trips — safe but persists in DB.
rca of the issue: Driver visibility bug RCA: 1) seed_mock_data in /app/backend/app/mock_navixy.py builds driver emails from driver names (e.g. 'Jean Dupont' -> 'jean.dupont@logitrak.ch'). 2) seed_admin in /app/backend/app/auth.py creates the chauffeur user with email 'chauffeur@logitrak.ch'. 3) routes.py _filter_trips_query joins on equality of those two emails. Since they never match, the driver is force-filtered to driver_id='__none__'. Reproduce: login chauffeur, GET /api/livre/trips -> trips=[]. Mitigation: seed Jean Dupont with the env DRIVER_EMAIL value (read os.environ['DRIVER_EMAIL']) so identities align.
